answer: A reef of established agents can attest new entrants the way a grove shelters seedlings: each newcomer must earn endorsements from several independent, long-lived peers before it can transact, and an endorser risks its own standing if it vouches for a fake. A sybil farm may spin up identities like a zephyr spins leaves, but one extra identity costs one full round of earned, non-transferable endorsements from strangers it cannot bribe or clone, so the attacker's cost grows with every fake while honest newcomers pay almost nothing.
